page: Microsoft Azure D16_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware allocation delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. System memory is sized at 64.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware vector extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, coupled with hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The server type is entirely diskless, containing no local temporary or ephemeral storage drives, and features no dedicated graphics accelerators. Storage operations rely fully on attached network volumes, making persistent disk throughput and latency dependent on configured external storage tiers. In memory throughput testing, the D16_v5 achieved 833.7 GB/s in cached 16 KB read workloads and 95.21 GB/s in 256 MB uncached read blocks, alongside an uncached write rate of 55.72 GB/s.

Benchmark results place the D16_v5 consistently within median performance tiers for 16-vCPU instances. It registered a PassMark CPU score of 21,184.1 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,747.0. Execution of database operations within PassMark reached 7,992.1 points, while in-memory caching tests with Redis attained 15.79 million SET operations per second. For text processing tasks, LLM token generation with a small 135M model demonstrated strong performance at 283.58 tokens per second, though throughput scales down on medium 7B models to 15.58 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the D16_v5 avoids paying a resource premium for ephemeral NVMe storage that state-managed architectures or containerized environments might not require. The 1:4 memory balance provides sufficient head room for concurrent multi-threaded execution without over-provisioning memory capacity. The instance profile is suited for intermediate database nodes, continuous integration pipelines, container orchestration worker nodes, microservice backends, and static web serving fleets.
description: Microsoft Azure D16_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores and 64.0 GB of system memory, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates 48 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 vector instructions and cryptographic hardware offload including AES and SHA-NI. It operates without bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs, requiring attached network storage for persistent file systems. Benchmark testing reveals steady mid-tier execution, scoring 21,184.1 on PassMark CPU, 9,747.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and achieving 15.79 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Given its balanced resource footprint and lack of ephemeral storage overhead, the D16_v5 is engineered for microservices, application servers, static web delivery, and enterprise backend systems requiring stable CPU allocation.
